items.title: 战争机器：E-Day 回顾——精彩的射击提振了低迷的战役
items.summary: Gears has never felt better to play, or more creatively stagnant.

content.v: What is it? A prequel to the classic third-person cover shooters Release date: October 6, 2026 Expect to pay: $70/£60 Developer: The Coalition Publisher: Xbox Game Studios Reviewed on: Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 Steam Deck: TBA Link: Official site

What's the most stunning revelation in this Gears of War prequel? Marcus Fenix used to have a jump button. Yes, the king of cover-based shooting, a man more rooted to the ground than a scarecrow, spent his youth jumping to some bits of cover. So E-Day contains at least one literal leap forward for the franchise. Shame it's trapped in a slog of a campaign that's otherwise anything but.

But before I moan about that, plenty of good news first. Gears has never felt better to play. These third-person cover shooters have always been a blast when they're working, and a miserable swearing fit when you dodge roll into certain death instead of snapping into cover like you wanted to. Again.

That nonsense has finally been excised, mostly, thanks to slightly more acrobatic characters and some wise button remapping. It's amazing what a difference sticking run on L3 and giving climb its own designated button makes.

Gears of War's biggest haters are liable to characterise its cover-shooting as a dull game of whack-a-mole. Perhaps on Normal difficulty, but Hardcore is where the experience sings. Here, staying in the same spot of cover is rightfully punished. You've got to keep gaining better ground, constantly weighing up the risks of lining up a sniper shot, a chainsaw insta-kill, or making a desperate dash for cover. It's a turn-based tactics shooter with a missing pause button. There's a reason that it translated so smoothly to a tactics spin-off.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/NWKQowBbPLibMZHh4LMCsM-1920-80.jpg

E-Day introduces new weaponry that makes cowering in cover harder than ever. It loves a blast of acid, this game, either delivered from a massive evil frog or a new gun that shotguns it at you. Devastating, but a loving kiss on the cheek compared to the Goreshot, a grappling hook only interested in grappling your torso from your body. So gloriously over-the-top, it almost makes up for the insta-kill tedium from the elite enemy who wields it.

That stuff's good, but it's the renovations to the old guard that stand out. The spike trap now opens with a hugely satisfying thunk-thunk-thunk as its horrible insides prepare themselves for a good gouging. The explosive arrow-firing torque bow gets a great glow up—the sound design as it finds its target is wonderful, practically a doomsday drum roll, so good I still enjoy it even when a locust is aiming it at me. And if I'm ever called upon to assassinate God, this game's sublime sniper rifle is what I'm reaching for.
So if the gunplay's a treat and the core combat never better, what's the problem? Well, almost everything else, unfortunately.
Dis-may

E-Day is a prequel, referring to the fateful day when the locust got bored of living underground and burst free from the surface to say a very messy hello. This is covered in the opening cutscene of the original Gears of War. And if you're wondering what insights E-Day has that weren't covered in said cutscene, same here.

The game opens with Marcus Fenix and Dom 'boy isn't it great that my wife and kids are alive' Santiago. Instead of the cynical, traumatised, seen-it-all-before combat veteran of the original Gears, here Marcus is… a cynical, traumatised, seen-it-all-before combat veteran. Oh.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/AedJ9GyGYQr4sBhybxB9Rc-1920-80.jpg

Discovering Marcus was once a flamboyant drag queen who was changed forever by E-Day into the man we know today was probably too much to hope for. But the fact he's essentially exactly the frikkin' same is the first alarm bell that this prequel is struggling to justify its own existence.
Is the shooting strong enough to sustain this? Yeah, just, though it does get exhausting.

Once the locust arrive, E-Day tries cosplaying as Resident Evil for a bit, complete with a trip through the panicking city to the police station. Some of these horror moments work. The drone gets an excellent introduction, though not so much for the poor sap stuck in the interrogation room with it. Other attempts at horror atmosphere are hilariously clumsy. I find the blood-soaked helmet of a transit worker, and the game immediately shatters any sense of foreboding with text popping up saying 'Bloody Transit Worker's Helmet Found!' Er, hooray?

The game then has some dumb fun giving little origin stories to its iconography—chainsaws being attached to machine guns! Grenades being tossed in emergence holes! Problem is, by the start of Act 2, you have the weaponry, armor, and the squad. At which point E-Day just becomes standard Gears of War again. You explore the ruined city (not open-world, more wide-ish linear) with goals never more complicated than 'shoot those locusts' or 'survive this wave of locusts' or 'why haven't you shot those locusts yet?'
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gbeWTpkCZx7ABhNBW3uFqM-1920-80.jpg

Gears 5 understood the value of variety. It had sections where you had to stealth around a mad scientist's factory to stealth kill infected robots. Or ride a skiff down an icy mountain. Or fight an enemy on the stage of a Hamilton-inspired musical which starts rotating at the worst moment possible (play Gears 5— it's one of the best 7/10s ever ).

True, not all of Gears 5's ideas worked. But I wanted a sequel that improved upon them, not a regression that believes the only thing you should ever be doing in one of these games is endlessly pulling the trigger. It's just slightly remixed combat encounters all the way down. Battle a giant frog and several snipers! OK, now two frogs, one sniper, and several shotgunners! OK, OK, now three giant spiders that fire insta-kill rockets, and loads of grunts, and the last checkpoint was seven minutes back! …Hey, why are you suddenly aiming at me?

Is the shooting strong enough to sustain this? Yeah, just, though it does get exhausting. It's an action movie with everything ripped out that isn't bullets going into bastards. The 20+ hour campaign is also waaaaay too long considering how one-note it is (well, aside from two crap shooting-from-a-turret-inside-a-helicopter bits, but I was planning on being nice and not bringing those up).
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YLDDyo4amfy7iL68E6AdaM-1920-80.jpg
Moderate improvements

New for E-Day are mod slots for your weapons and armour. Mods include less recoil, better scopes, faster chainsaw revving, etc. Not as useless and incremental as the crap you get in [insert whichever live service shooter you currently have the most beef with here], but it's borderline and hard to get excited about. Far better is the gizmo that can send out rippling shockwaves that stun enemies, perfect for a chainsawin'. I found a mod for it that also sets enemies on fire. Lovely.

You get these mods for completing sidequests or finding them in cases. But E-Day is so terrified of you missing anything that tiresome all-caps text saying HARD CASE NEARBY blazes across the screen. And the location of the case is immediately added to your map. Oh and if you activate whatever this game's version of Eagle Vision is called, we'll show you exactly where the case is. Ugh.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/QTw5uxM3qZ8DMTspriukhM-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/5b9h8ZA8QENTiG3DRedwzL-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/e7ZY84pA5esCCevLTML5KR-1920-80.jpg

items.title: Razer 的 Wolverine V4 控制器对于大多数游戏玩家来说太过分了，这就是重点
items.summary: Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for

content.v: Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for Xbox and PC. Geared toward competitive gamers--not that there's anything stopping you from using it to play Vampire Survivors--and it focuses primarily on polling performance and thumbstick sensor architecture.

One of the biggest changes is Razer choosing capacitive contactless sensors backed by a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for the thumbsticks, rather than the usual Hall Effect magnetic sensor. While Hall Effect thumbsticks are popular for their durability and for essentially eliminating stick drift, they can be prone to magnetic interference. Not a dealbreaker if you're playing at home, but in a competitive scene where victory is measured in fractions of a second, this can be an issue. In comparison, Razer is aiming to offer the same drift resistance, finer granularity, and smoother signal tracking with capacitive sensing.

Then there's the polling rate, which is absurdly high. For example, a DualSense Edge is capable of offering up to 1,000Hz (1 ms to 8 ms input latency), but the Wolverine V4 pushes that number up to 8,000Hz in both its wired and wireless configurations when used on PC, which, in theory, should put that on par with high-end esports mice and keyboards. This isn't the first Razer controller to feature an 8,000Hz polling rate, as the Wolverine V3 Pro was also equipped to reach those numbers.
Just don't expect to reach those levels on Xbox Series X|S, as hardware limitations cap the refresh rate at 250Hz, meaning the 8,000Hz benefit is strictly for PC competitive gaming.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Wolverine-1.jpg?w=636
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Wolverine-3.jpg?w=636
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Wolverine-4.jpg?w=636
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Wolverine-5.jpg?w=636
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Wovlerine-2.jpg?w=636

The controller also offers four removable magnetic back buttons and two top claw-grip bumpers, with a modular magnetic design that lets players quickly swap components out, stripping the controller of unused buttons and extra weight. First-person shooter players can also use a back-mounted physical toggle switch with software-tunable actuation points, allowing them to fine-tune the hair-trigger click threshold.

That makes for a solid controller on paper, even if you don't need all of its features. The wireless model has an MSRP of $200, making it a little bit more expensive than the Xbox Elite Series 2 wireless controller and on par with the DualSense Edge (which can also be used on PC). If you'd prefer a wired option, the Wolverine V4 wired version will set you back $100.

Another controller worth keeping an eye on is the recently revealed Genki Manta . Genki launched a Kickstarter campaign for it, raising over $1.1 million for a peripheral that combines high customizability with an OLED display. The company aims to launch it next year, with an MSRP of $279.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/06/best-pokemon-tcg-deals-prime-day-1791305050250.png

Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale is now fully underway, and there are more than enough standout offers to get your teeth stuck into over the next couple of days. Yes, this is a remarkably short sale by Amazon's recent standards, lasting just 48 hours through October 6-7.
There are a few new Pokémon TCG items that have been restocked as part of the sale, including 30th anniversary First Partner Collections, Surging Sparks, and Perfect Order boosters, and loads more.
The selection isn't quite as spectacular as we've seen in previous restocks, such as during Pokémon Day or Labor Day, but it's still not bad at all. Let's take a look at what's up for grabs.

For now, let's start with the biggest and best finds from this Labor Day restock. Pokémon TCG's First Partner Illustration Collection Series 3 is part of Pokémon's 30th anniversary celebrations. This release marks the final chapter in the First Partner Illustration TCG Collection.

Series 1 took us back to the classic roots with Kanto (Gen 1), Sinnoh (Gen 4), and Alola (Gen 7). Series 2 took us back to the Johto (Gen 2), Unova (Gen 5), and Galar (Gen 8) regions. Series 3 officially rounds out the whole collection, bringing us the beloved first partner Pokémon from the Hoenn, Kalos, and Paldea regions.

Listed median prices for these is $34 at TCGplayer , which is bang on what Amazon is listing it for as well. Average market price is around $30-$35 (not including delivery), so Amazon is probably your best bet for these, especially if you're picking up two or three, and even more so if you're an Amazon Prime member with free speedy delivery.
Same as the other two series, inside each box, you'll score:

Amazon currently has the 30th Celebration ETB listed for just $159.99 , considerable up from the $89.99 price we spotted previously. A bit annoying for those who missed out on the better deal, but Amazon having stock and still allowing invites is better than absolutely nothing.

The timing here is worth paying attention to. When we first spotted Amazon taking invite requests at below $90, the 30th Celebration set hadn't yet fully hit the market. Now that the 30th Anniversary collection is officially out, we're seeing just how difficult some of its products can be to find at a reasonable price .

The bigger problem is that requesting an invite doesn't mean Amazon will actually offer you the ETB , even if you are willing to pay the $160. The retailer previously introduced invite requests for this product in the US, an unusual move given that Amazon's US Pokémon TCG listings have traditionally been priced much closer to prevailing market prices.

Amazon also has the rare Surging Sparks boosters back in stock at what is an eye watering $17.59 per booster pack. Yeesh. TCGplayer is running these for below $10 still, so you may be better off buying from a third-party reseller in all honestly. But, the option is there at Amazon, along with all the other products in the restock, if you so desire.

But is it worth it? Only you can be the judge of that. The "market price" is often dictated by what the majority of people are willing to pay, but only you can decide if this if truely worth your money.
No matter how unfortunate it is, and how hard it is to find Pokémon TCG at MSRP , market value is often the price you have to pay now, even from big retailers like Amazon, as I mentioned.
To see all the recently restocked items at Amazon, be sure to check out our custom search tracker to ensure you're buying sealed boosters that are only "sold and shipped" directly from Amazon itself.
IGN is the best place to find TCG deals

IGN's resident deals experts like Robert Anderson have over seven years of experience writing about gaming and TCG deals. In an era where finding advice from a real person is more important than ever, Robert’s expertise helps you cut through the digital noise to find genuine, money-saving offers. He pairs his experience and love of games with data-driven analysis and price-tracking tools to ensure he's only ever recommending something that's actually worthwhile.

If you're looking some no-nonsense help on saving money in a time where gaming and TCG hobbies have never been more expensive, then we'd highly recommend following him @robertliam21 on Bluesky and setting IGN as a preferred source in Google to make sure you're getting the latest updates, from him, and the rest of the IGN Shopping team.

items.title: 《战地 6》通过标记挑逗复活死亡空间的尸体
items.summary: The corpse of Dead Space is being reinimated for Battlefield 6, with the latest trailer for Season 5 seemingly

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/06/battlefield-dead-space-1791301809536.png
The corpse of Dead Space is being reinimated for Battlefield 6 , with the latest trailer for Season 5 seemingly teasing a crossover.

Battlefield 6’s new trailer shows off a new Las Vegas map that looks like a lot of fun, as choppers and machine guns tear up casinos and skyscrapers along The Strip. But then the music fades out, ominous sounds creep in, and it cuts to a bloom-filled scene where two Dead Space engineers stare up at The Marker, the survival horror series’ alien artifact that drills into your brain.

Earlier this year, series writer Chuck Beaver claimed sales were too low for EA to greenlight a Dead Space 4 . Series co-creator and developer of The Callisto Protocol, Glen Schofield, also retired from the industry this year after his spiritual successor failed to light up the industry.

Battlefield 6 players on Reddit already spotted potential Dead Space skins, which were rumored to launch in the Halloween update this October, so that’s probably what you can expect. Developers at Dice have previously gone on the record to say Battlefield 6 won’t feature goofy, immersion breaking skins . That’s done now, if these rumors are true.

EA recently added a Dead Space skin to Skate and charged $40 for it so there's precedent for skins in the universe. Players weren’t happy with the skin itself or the cost, so it’ll be interesting to see if EA aims for more realistic pricing for the next crossover. Battlefield 6 previously did a crossover event with Top Gun , but that makes sense in a game featuring fighter jets.
Battlefield 6’s fifth Season features three new maps, including Vegas Strip and Area 51, six new weapons and two new vehicles. You can jump into Vegas on October 13.

As for Dead Space, talking on the FRVR Podcast , Beaver said that to recoup the costs of the franchise's high production values, any new game would need to sell over 10 million copies — a tall order for even a breakout horror game.

“Any of the Resident Evils are selling around seven million [copies], that’s a pretty good number," Beaver said. "But, you know, companies now are looking for the next Fortnite . They need something that is a perennial moneymaker… something like a single-player package game with no live-service offering that’s like it’s just a dinosaur fossil of a business model."

The Dead Space remake, developed by EA-owned Motive Studio and released in 2023, was well-received but appears to have not done enough business to convince the powers that be at the mega publisher to invest in a follow-up. IGN's Dead Space remake review returned a 9/10. We said: "Dead Space is a superb remake and undoubtedly the definitive way to experience one of the best survival horror shooters that Capcom never made."

“Horror games have a bit of a ceiling, you know, and I think the number back in [former EA VP] Frank Gibeau’s day was 5 million units to keep going on Dead Space," Beaver continued. "I think the number is like 15 million units now, given the cost of things," he added, before joking that it was "a sadness in capitalism for all of us to suffer, until AI makes it apparently easy for you and I just type 'make Dead Space 4.'"

In October last year, Schofield told IGN he hoped to bring the franchise back to life , despite EA's lack of interest. “I went to [EA] recently and they're like, 'No, we're not interested anymore,'” he said. “I said, 'I can get back the leadership team. I need the models from EA Motive and I can save you 30 to 40 million dollars on the idea that I have.' And, they're like, 'No.'"

“I have quite a few ideas that I'm ready to go with and one of them is Dead Space 4,” Schofield continued. “The fact that EA just got bought, I think there’s an opportunity. I’m already making calls.”

items.title: 诺兰·诺斯 (Nolan North) 保持健康状态，以防索尼致电《神秘海域 5》
items.summary: Uncharted star Nolan North is keen to return for Uncharted 5, amid reports that a fresh entry in the franchise

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/06/gettyimages-1162869055-1791306580444.jpg
Uncharted star Nolan North is keen to return for Uncharted 5, amid reports that a fresh entry in the franchise is in production .

While Sony is yet to officially announce any new Uncharted project, Naughty Dog has confirmed it has multiple games in the works right now. Aside from the upcoming Intergalactic: Heretic Prophet, it is believed that Uncharted: The Lost Legacy director Shaun Escayg is leading a team building a fresh entry in the company's beloved adventure series.

North, who portrays Uncharted hero Nathan Drake, has now said he would happily return to the role if asked — and has even tried to stay in shape for whenever the call comes. Perhaps unsurprisingly, North is also bullish on Uncharted 5's likelihood of success if it is indeed released — while also acknowledging that Naughty Dog needed to avoid launching something as unpopular as the fourth Indiana Jones movie, Kingdom of the Crystal Skull.

"I think it would be one of the biggest games ever if they decided to do it," North said, speaking during the Gamergy show in Puerto Rico (thanks, DomTheBomb / VGC ). "It just depends if Sony wants to make money.

"I haven't heard anything, but you know, it is a business and my God, can you imagine if they if they did? I mean, it would be the biggest announcement in gaming. And I don’t think that’s hyperbole, I think that's true. I think that would be... to bring back a storied franchise like that? You just don't want to make a Kingdom of the Crystal Skull."

While Intergalactic is believed to be the next project to launch from Naughty Dog, the studio still has a legion of fans keen for new entries in its other franchises: The Last of Us and Uncharted. It's now been a decade since Uncharted 4 released and put a nice bow on Nathan Drake's adventures, but this gap in time also opens up the possibility of a fresh adventure that featured his daughter, Cassie.
"You know, I try to stay in shape, just in case," Nolan concluded. "It was 10 years of work with good friends, good people, a great developer. I can't see a scenario that I would say no."
Photo by Albert L. Ortega/Getty Images.

items.title: 《极限竞速：地平线 6》的社区厌倦了 Playground 游戏，工作室终于做出了回应
items.summary: Forza Horizon 6 developer Playground Games has finally addressed its player community after months of construc

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/06/assets-2026-01-1769110937-fh6-screenshots-06-cover-car-mt-fuji-1791306463001.jpg

Forza Horizon 6 developer Playground Games has finally addressed its player community after months of constructive feedback about the game has been met with nothing but radio silence from the renowned British studio.

"Hey Horizon Community," the post on the studio's social channels begins, "We're reading all your comments about Forza Horizon 6, and we realize that we haven't been talking with you as much as we could be. While we continue to deliver regular content and fixes into the game, we want you to know we hear your feedback about our post-launch updates and we're looking into future changes to both in-game content and the ways we communicate with you. Stay tuned!"

Forza Horizon 6 got rave reviews upon its release – including a 10 out of 10 from IGN – but Playground's lack of communication with its players has frustrated the community. As detailed in videos from Forza Horizon content creators STEVIO2175 , AR12Gaming , HokiHoshi , and Ericship 111 , players are upset at the live service game's complete absence of communication from Playground as well as some features from previous Forza games that are missing from the newest Horizon.

"It just feels like the community engagement between the developers and us is just nonexistent," STEVIO2175 said in his excellent and thorough 19-minute video on the subject from late August. Players are feeling like they have to spend their time in the Horizon Festival playlists in order to get access to the new cars – many of which are recycled from previous Horizon games – rather than play in whatever modes and ways they want.

Playground's Forza Monthly show that directly interfaces with the community has also been absent, leading some in the Forza space to wonder if it's a side effect of new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's big " reset " and subsequent layoffs. The lack of in-game voice chat in Horizon 6 is also on the community's list of constructive criticisms – a particularly curious omission from FH6 given that the previous entry in the Forza series, 2023's Forza Motorsport, has voice chat to this day. "Voice chat alone could make FH6 Japan ten times better," STEVIO2175 said. "But the thing that bothers me most at the end of the day," he added, "is that the devs have not responded at all. No communication, no public responses, nothing."

More to the point, STEVIO2175 said he believes that most players don't feel like this game has replayability past single player. "Until the socialization and community features get added, if they ever do, player interest is going to continue to drop," STEVIO2175 said. "And I hope they figure this all out before PS5 hopefully still gets this game."

On that note, Microsoft and Playground still have not announced a release date for the PlayStation 5 version of Forza Horizon 6 despite it being October now and the last the companies said , it'd ship on PS5 this year. That looks increasingly unlikely by the day, but perhaps it's for the best if Playground needs to iron out all of its communication and content roadmap criticisms from the community before launching on another platform.

A second team at Playground is also in the stretch run of development on the Fable reboot, which is due to be released on Xbox, PC, and PS5 on February 23, 2027. It's fair to wonder if Fable has been pulling resources away from Forza Horizon 6 as the former team makes its final sprint to the finish line. We finally got to play Fable at Gamescom in August and were quite pleased by the combat .

items.title: 我在 GTA 5 中添加了骗局，但我可能骗了自己
items.summary: At least I have a stylish new bag.

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

A shift in the fabric of reality: I launch Grand Theft Auto 5 and, following the now-customary hitch-and-stutter loading screen that can last anywhere from 10 seconds to five minutes, Franklin spawns into his familiar void apartment. Within seconds, he begins plummeting, screaming.
All of this is fine and normal.

But something new: Franklin carries a duffel bag with him into the abyss now, and I am unsure as to why. My guess is that it is a byproduct of my newly installed mod, ScamV , which "turns Los Santos into your digital playground." Let the possibilities unfurl ahead of you—"Take on the role of a cyber-criminal, exploit vulnerabilities, use cloned cards, and build your underground fortune."

Mostly, though, it has given me a bag. Don't get me wrong, I am sure that all of these things would be present in a regular installation of ScamV, but unfortunately ScamV in my world is forced to compete with an armageddon of other mods: the flying cars, new interiors, deleted exteriors, credit ratings and so on.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YgttpG9GpP8tFrimUtaEDG-1920-80.gif

So mostly it is a bag. But wait, there is also this—the possibility of walking into a bank, any bank, and interacting with the teller by paying in fake cheques. "You don't have any fake cheques," the game tells me when I attempt this. It does not tell me where or how to obtain them. Kafka-esque. Five stars.

content.v: Few things are constant in life, but the reminder that AI is wriggling its way into just about every facet of life is unfortunately pervasive. Take games for example, it's wormed its way into voice acting , voice acting , and more voice acting. But aside from giving players a plethora of dull and generic quips it's also been cited as one of the reasons behind the seemingly neverending string of layoffs in the industry.

The thought process is 'why pay humans to do work when you can pay robots to do it, just kind of worse.' This is where Warhorse's co-founder, Martin Klima, thinks videogame execs are getting it wrong, because "AI is not a get out of jail free card."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MajZ6PCV3dyVXUzYp3D4aB-1920-80.jpg
While Klima does believe that AI may become unavoidable if cost-saving stays as important as it already is, he points out that "it doesn't work how people imagine in a very simplified mental model".

The idea that you can lay off half your staff and replace them with AI is a "fundamentally flawed idea, because it doesn't work like that". Klima believes that instead of replacing half of a team of devs, player demand for bigger and bigger games will invariably drive studios to keep their human dev teams the same size, but augmented by AI. This would, he says, allow them to make even bigger games than they could beforehand. The game that offers players more "is going to be better".

"It can mean [the game] has more branching classes," Klima adds. "It can mean it has more missions to play, whatever—people will still want to have this bigger game." While AI may not reduce the cost of the game, it will allow us to create bigger games for the same cost".

Some studios have been using machine learning to cut out busy work that only bogs its developers down for a while now, like Warcraft . Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick also commented on the tech, saying that, while AI isn't in the business of making hits because "clones don't sell", it can still be helpful to devs . Unfortunately, it looks like not everyone's got the memo just yet.
